entrypoints.summary: The audit finding identifies the BoringSSL-backed ECDH path that receives Go private and public ECDH wrapper objects containing C pointers.
ECDH(priv, pub) passes wrapper-owned C key material and point state to cgo/BoringCrypto operations.

affected_components.role: Go ECDH wrappers free C allocations through finalizers; ECDH invokes BoringCrypto using their C pointers and the inspected present-state source retains both wrappers through the call.

causal_paths.kind: Go finalizer / cgo native pointer lifetime

code_slices.fixed: The inspected unpinned source defers runtime.KeepAlive(priv) and runtime.KeepAlive(pub) in ECDH.
code_slices.surrounding_context: Both wrapper types have finalizers that free their C allocations, and source comments state that cgo use of such pointers must be followed by runtime.KeepAlive.
code_slices.vulnerable: The audit reports an ECDH path lacking the required post-cgo object-liveness retention; the exact vulnerable revision is not included in the bundle.

sources.concept: Go finalizer freeing wrapper-owned C ECDH memory during cgo execution

impact.affected_asset: C EC_KEY and EC_POINT allocations owned by Go ECDH wrapper objects during the C call.
impact.attacker_capability: No attacker-controlled exploitation capability is demonstrated by the supplied audit material; it identifies a caller-reachable API-level lifetime condition.
impact.security_effect: Potential timing-dependent native-memory use-after-free in the BoringCrypto-backed ECDH computation.

causal_trace.summary: PublicKeyECDH and PrivateKeyECDH wrappers own C EC point/key pointers and install Go finalizers that free those C allocations.

If a wrapper's last Go-level reference is consumed while its C pointer is in a cgo call, garbage collection may run its finalizer before that C call returns; the audit describes this as freeing memory at the start of a C function call using it.
The ECDH path supplies the private-key-derived state and public point to the BoringCrypto EC_POINT_mul cgo call while those underlying allocations must remain live.

The resulting timing-dependent condition is potential native-memory use-after-free during the C ECDH call; the supplied artifacts do not establish a crash, exploitation, or a specific confidentiality or integrity outcome.

failure.operation: BoringCrypto EC_POINT_mul cgo call on wrapper-owned ECDH key/point state after premature finalizer-driven freeing

primary_invariant.statement: Every Go wrapper whose finalizer frees C key or point memory must remain live until every cgo call using its C pointer has returned.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A Go finalizer can free the wrapper-owned C allocation while the in-flight C operation still uses the pointer unless an explicit post-call liveness boundary retains the wrapper.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit and inspected source establish the reported cross-runtime lifetime mechanism and KeepAlive restoration pattern. The public source locator is unpinned and already contains KeepAlive calls, so it is evidence of the intended protection rather than proof of a vulnerable current revision. No pinned vulnerable Go revision, fixing commit, regression test, GC/finalizer scheduling trace, sanitizer output, crash, or exploit result is included; no executable oracle is claimed.

remediation.invariant_restored: Defer runtime.KeepAlive for each ECDH wrapper after the cgo work so its finalizer cannot free wrapper-owned C memory before the C call completes.
mitigation_classes: explicit Go-object liveness retention across cgo calls

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Trail of Bits report published March 27, 2025; the supplied report artifact is pinned in trailofbits/publications commit 68408ccfe7600935cea71dbf7b5c930f7ea3a8d0. The audited Go source revision is not supplied.
